CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR
ORAL ORDER

The petitioner has been convicted for the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, and sentenced to life imprisonment.

sentences.text:
2. The petitioner has approached this Court seeking a direction to respondent No.2 to release him on parole on the grounds that:
(i) He needs to oversee the repair work of his house, which is in a dilapidated condition and where his family is currently residing.
(ii) He needs to provide care and support for his aged mother, including facilitating her medical treatment.
The petitioner has already served more than four years and two months of his sentence as of the date of filing this petition, and it is noted that he has not been released on parole previously.
4. Considering the circumstances and the grounds put forth, the petitioner has established a prima facie case for being granted parole.

Accordingly, I pass the following:

sentences.text: ORDER a.
The Writ Petition is allowed.

b. Respondent No.2 is hereby directed to release the convict in CTP No.12350 on parole for a period of 90 days from the date of release, subject to petitioner undertaking not to involve in unlawful activities during the period of parole.

c. Respondent No.2 shall impose strict conditions as are usually stipulated to ensure the return of the detenue to the jail and the convict shall not commit any other offence during the period of parole.
d. Violation of any of the parole conditions would result in cancellation of parole.
e. Liberty is reserved with the petitioner to seek extension of parole, if permissible in law.
The Registry is directed to communicate this order to respondent No.2, by way of electronic mail, forthwith.

Sd/-
